extraction.NOTES: Cover letter dated December 18, 1923, from Pine Ridge Agency, Pine Ridge, So. Dak., signed by E. W. Jermark, Superintendent, to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Written in compliance with Circular No. 2464 and letter of December 4, 1928. Eleven affidavits enclosed regarding forced patents. Patents were delivered by mailing a receipt to the Indian with a letter; if the receipt was not signed and returned within a reasonable time, the Indian was notified that the issuance had been reported to the State Tax Commission. References U.S. vs. County of Benewah and U.S. vs. County of Kootenai (Circuit Court of Appeals, 9th Circuit). Records at the County Seat were taken only to the time the Indian relinquished title; a clerk could average about ten to twelve patents per day after becoming familiar with records in the office of the Register of Deeds. | TASK 5 RECLASSIFICATION 2026-05-03: This record was originally enumerated as CAT_1 (Sonnet missed allottee Name + Allotment), but it is NOT an allottee record — it is a cover letter from E.W.
